clue.text: Vegetable makes sleep sweeter

wordplay.note: read as a verb and its object: 'sugars' means makes sweeter, and a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A claim that eating some vegetable gives you sweeter dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SUGARS + NAP: to sugar something is to make it sweeter, and the thing sweetened is a nap, or sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar snap is a variety of pea eaten pod and all, a common green vegetable.

clue.text: Dismisses British neurologist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fires from a job
second meaning: Oliver ..., the British-born neurologist and author of The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a scientist being sacked; the two parts are independent meanings of one name-word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to fire them, and Oliver Sacks was a famous British neurologist and writer.

clue.text: Sweet cake allowed to be consumed by spectators

indicators.note: something consumed ends up inside the eater, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sporting event
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A dessert the crowd at a match is permitted to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the gate is the attendance at a match, or the money it pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A galette is a flat round French cake or pastry, often sweet.

clue.text: Country demoting the leader in downfall

indicators.note: demoting moves the first letter down the line, so it goes to a later place in the word

parts.note: a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A nation's fall from power after its ruler is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The I that leads IRAN drops two places, giving RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a fall of rain or snow, so the word is a literal meteorological synonym.

clue.text: Unsophisticated in turning up embracing a fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A naive person arriving with their arm around a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The container step happens first, and only then is that short chunk turned up; the fellow is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif is an adjective (and noun) meaning naive or artless, which is unsophisticated.

clue.text: Possibly fine component of shrubbery in which there's a particular spot

definitions.text: in which there's a particular spot

parts.note: a fine is one kind of penalty, hence 'possibly'
box is a shrub much used in hedges and shrubberies

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a nice bit of hedge with a particular spot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The particular spot is the penalty spot, which lies inside a football pitch's penalty box.
explanation.definitionFit: The penalty area of a football pitch, also called the penalty box, contains the penalty spot from which penalty kicks are taken.

clue.text: Old Irish families providing short items for certain calendar pages?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clans or family branches in old Ireland

definitions.text: short items for certain calendar pages
definitions.meaning: second meaning: abbreviations of September, as printed at the top of a month's page

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: the September page of a calendar is headed with the short form of its month.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a clan or division of a family, especially in Ireland, and Sept is the standard abbreviation of September.

clue.text: Random person not readily moved to accept Charles Trenet at first

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the other parts go inside

parts.note: a stoic endures without showing emotion
Chas is a traditional short form of Charles

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the initial of the French singer's surname

explanation.surface: An unemotional person making room for the French crooner Charles Trenet.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Trenet was a French singer, best known for 'La Mer'; only his surname's initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Stochastic is the technical term for something governed by chance or randomly determined.

clue.text: Religious figure in decline turned up in burial site of kings

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so the order of letters flips
the word in places one part inside the other

parts.note: a dip is a decline or fall
the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A holy statue in a sunken spot being dug up from a royal tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious figure' suggests a statue or cleric; here it is the mother of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids were built as tombs for pharaohs, the kings of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Petition for zone around North African location at first — this one?

definitions.text: Petition for zone around North African location at first — this one?

parts.note: to sue is to petition a court
Z is the abbreviation for zone
ca. abbreviates circa, around
N is the abbreviation for North

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the words it follows

parts.note: the initials of the two words

explanation.surface: A request for the territory surrounding a North African site, with a hint that the site is this answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the waterway's zone in Egypt was famously fought over, and the clue ends asking whether it is the very location meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal is the waterway across Egypt in North Africa, whose surrounding zone was the subject of disputes and claims.

clue.text: College is following plan to get around one path to disaster

indicators.note: getting around something means surrounding it, so it sits inside

parts.note: Coll. is the abbreviation for college
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a project that follows its plan is said to be on course

explanation.surface: A university is sticking to a plan in order to get round a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for one lands between the second and third chunks, so the first three pieces of wordplay together surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision course is a trajectory that will inevitably end in a crash, figuratively a road to conflict or ruin.

clue.text: Popular film is back in place

indicators.note: back means turned round, read from the end towards the start

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's hugely popular film about an alien
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-liked movie is being shown again where it belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the place where something is or happens.

clue.text: Claim he transmuted carbon — hoping for gold?

indicators.note: to transmute is to change into another form, so the letters change their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A would-be scientist boasts of changing carbon into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transmuted' and 'gold' both suit the alchemist's lab, so the anagram signal hides in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy sought chiefly to turn base metals into gold, so an alchemic enterprise is one hoping for gold.

clue.text: Lack of skill represented as immature

indicators.note: represented here means presented in a new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's incompetence is put down to childishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurism can mean the unprofessional, unskilled quality of work done without proper expertise.

clue.text: I get ecstatic, I start to admit — not bodily present?

parts.note: taken as written
to nab is to catch or get
sent is old slang for thrilled or in ecstasy
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: An excited confession that one's mind is elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The two I's in the clue each supply an I; 'sent' meaning enraptured is dated jazz slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In absentia is Latin for 'in absence', used of someone tried or awarded something while not physically there.

clue.text: Porter, perhaps — individual secured by my tip?

parts.note: porter is a dark type of beer, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it

parts.note: taken as written
one individual

explanation.surface: A hotel porter wonders whether a single coin will do for his tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like the hotel servant who gets tipped; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer money is a small gratuity, notionally enough to buy a drink, so a tip fits as an example.

clue.text: Nonsense from America about job pursuing record website content

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other parts go inside

parts.note: BS is American slang for nonsense

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the word before it follows the next one

parts.note: a log is a record
a post is a job

explanation.surface: An American dismisses as rubbish what a job hunter keeps online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonsense from America' is the polite way of citing a ruder Americanism by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Blog posts are the individual articles published on a weblog, a staple of website content.

clue.text: Editor probing hospital litter

indicators.note: probing means pushing into something, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
Ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist digging into rubbish at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but here it is the old sense of a carried chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, and a litter is the same kind of carried couch.

clue.text: Start working before being ready?

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go' or 'all set'

explanation.surface: A puzzle about beginning a job before everything is prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is a noun for the beginning or start of something, such as an illness.

clue.text: Flashed in street, wearing loose garment

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
someone wearing a robe is robed

explanation.surface: A flasher in the street in his dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a flasher, but 'Flashed' means lit by pulses of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobed means lit with a strobe, a lamp that flashes rapidly and repeatedly.

clue.text: I brought in people with US railway fuel

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so one part goes within another

parts.note: bodies are people, as in 'a few warm bodies'
taken as written
the El is the elevated railway of US cities like Chicago

explanation.surface: Someone recounts adding passengers to an American train service.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago's elevated railway is called the El, a convention American clues lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodiesel is a fuel for diesel engines made from vegetable oils or animal fats.

clue.text: Upset is limiting blooming options for study

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top
limiting something means hemming it in on both sides, so it sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
bally is a dated British euphemism for bloody, like blooming

explanation.surface: A student is annoyed at limits on their choices of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' is not about flowers: it is a mild British intensifier, like 'bloody' toned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabi are outlines of courses, setting out the topics a student may choose to study.

clue.text: Judge, after hesitation, blocking less contaminated source of dodgy evidence

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, inside the other part

parts.note: purer means cleaner, less contaminated

indicators.note: after places the first word's letters following those of the next

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A courtroom judge pauses over tainted evidence from an unreliable source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' and 'evidence' set a courtroom scene, but the judge is just a one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A perjurer lies under oath, so the testimony they give is false or dodgy evidence.

clue.text: It's not enough for side dish

indicators.note: not enough means falling short, so the word is cut one letter before its end

parts.note: a flank is a side

explanation.surface: A complaint that a side dish is too meagre a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side dish' reads as a single phrase; split it, and side is the wordplay, dish the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry or sponge case with a filling, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Craving affection, with rise in desire after cuddling of Parisian

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, backwards
cuddling holds something close inside the arms, so one part goes within

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A clingy lover's longing grows as a French partner hugs them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Parisian' asks for the French word for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy describes someone emotionally demanding, who constantly wants attention and reassurance.

clue.text: Leader abandoning extra responsibility

indicators.note: the leader leaving means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bonus is something extra

explanation.surface: A boss walks out, leaving extra duties for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is Latin for burden and means a duty or responsibility, as in 'the onus is on you'.

clue.text: Comedian's eccentricity not OK when making sarcastic comment

indicators.note: not OK says those two letters are swapped out for the one the comedian's has instead

parts.note: a joker is a comedian
e is the symbol for eccentricity in maths and astronomy

explanation.surface: A comedian's oddball behaviour has gone too far, and the jibes sting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Comedian's' as 'comedian has': JOKER takes E in place of OK. Eccentricity of an orbit or conic is conventionally written e.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeer is a mocking, scornful remark, a sarcastic comment shouted at someone.

clue.text: Carry on after collapse of business etc, getting very little money

indicators.note: a collapse leaves things in disorder, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
to wage a war is to carry it on

explanation.surface: Staff keep going after their firm fails, on barely any pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places WAGE behind the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsistence wage is pay just enough to live on, so very little money.

clue.text: Party occupying most of a remarkable place for orgies and such

indicators.note: occupying a space means being inside it
most of means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: some can mean a remarkable, as in 'that was some party'
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A wild party taking over somewhere famously debauched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A remarkable' works as in 'that was some party!', where the word means remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, a byword for sexual debauchery.

clue.text: Ridiculous suggestion but diary's misinterpreted

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A silly idea arises because someone misread a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurdity is something ridiculous or nonsensical, such as a laughable proposal.
